summary: Adds an IMAP extension for creating live, automatically updated search results, something like virtual mailboxes. IMAP search is powerful, but the results are static and awkward to keep current. This standards-track extension lets a client define a context and be told as messages enter or leave it, so results stay current without re-running the search.

eli5.summary: It is like a saved search folder that updates by itself. Rather than asking the same question over and over, you ask once and the server taps you on the shoulder whenever the answer changes.

questions: what is the imap context extension
what does imap search return update do
subtitle: IMAP extensions that let a server push live changes to search and sort results and hand them out in windows.

tldr.problem: IMAP search results are static, and a huge mailbox can overwhelm the client's storage. Sorted results are hard to keep current on a changing mailbox over a slow connection.
tldr.mechanism: The ESORT and CONTEXT extensions add return options to SEARCH and SORT: UPDATE makes the server send ADDTO and REMOVEFROM notices as results change, PARTIAL returns a window of results, and CONTEXT hints that the search will be reused.
tldr.outcome: A client can show a live, filtered view of a mailbox, similar to a virtual mailbox, without re-running the search. RFC 5267 has been updated by RFC 5465 and RFC 9394.

today: RFC 5267 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 5465 and RFC 9394, so read those alongside it. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why IMAP Needs Contexts
sections.content:
The IMAP4rev1 protocol has powerful search built into its core. The basic SEARCH command, as improved by the ESEARCH extension, is compact, but the RFC notes that huge mailboxes might still overwhelm the storage available for results even on high-end desktop machines. The SORT command is useful, but hard to use well on changing mailboxes over low-bandwidth connections.

RFC 5267 borrows ideas from ACAP (RFC 2244), such as a windowed view onto search or sort results and bandwidth-efficient updates. It provides them through two extensions: ESORT and CONTEXT. The RFC also shows how they can give a facility like virtual mailboxes.
sections.eli5: If you keep a huge pile of letters, asking for a list of every red one is slow and the list goes stale. These extensions let the mailroom keep the list fresh for you.

sections.title: Extended SORT (ESORT)
sections.content:
A server that advertises the ESORT capability lets SORT and UID SORT take an optional list of return options after a RETURN atom, just as extended SEARCH does. Results come back in an ESEARCH response, always in the requested sort order. The options are MIN, MAX, ALL and COUNT. An empty list means ALL.

Ranges in these results MUST be in increasing numerical order after expansion, so 10:12 means the same as 12:10. To avoid confusion, servers SHOULD only write a range when the first number is lower than the second. In the RFC's example, a run of descending UIDs is therefore listed one by one rather than as a range.
sections.eli5: Sorting can now come back as a short summary, like just the count or just the first item, instead of the full list every time.

sections.title: Contexts and the Context Hint
sections.content:
A server supports contexts if its capabilities include CONTEXT=SEARCH and/or CONTEXT=SORT. CONTEXT=SORT servers also advertise SORT and support the extended SORT syntax. Each adds three search return options: CONTEXT, UPDATE and PARTIAL. They do not interact with each other or with the ESEARCH and ESORT options.

The CONTEXT option is a hint. A client SHOULD use it to say that it will likely reuse the same search criteria, and a server MAY ignore it or use it to maintain a full result cache or index. There is no snapshot facility: leaving out UPDATE or CONTEXT does not change what later searches return.

With CONTEXT=SEARCH the server orders all SEARCH results in mailbox order, by message number and UID. The command (SEARCH, UID SEARCH, SORT or UID SORT) is called the searching command and its order is the requested order.
sections.eli5: Saying CONTEXT is like telling the librarian that you will ask for this list again soon, so keep it handy if you want.

sections.title: Live Updates with UPDATE
sections.content:
If a client puts UPDATE in the return options, the server sends unsolicited ESEARCH responses carrying ADDTO and REMOVEFROM data items whenever the results of that search change. Reasons include new messages arriving, flags changing, or messages being expunged. The responses carry the tag of the searching command, so clients MUST NOT reuse tags. Reusing a tag that is already in use with an UPDATE search gets a BAD response.

Updates stop when the mailbox is no longer selected or when the client sends CANCELUPDATE with one or more tags. A server MAY refuse updates, for example at an internal limit, with an untagged NO carrying NOUPDATE and the tag, while still honoring the other options. Servers MUST provide at least one updating context per client.

ADDTO and REMOVEFROM each carry pairs of a context position and a set of results. The client MUST process them in order. A position of zero is allowed for SEARCH and UID SEARCH, and means the client may place the results so the list stays in mailbox order. A non-zero position inserts or removes at that spot. An ADDTO with message numbers MUST come after the EXISTS notice, and a REMOVEFROM with message numbers MUST come before the EXPUNGE.
sections.eli5: You tell the mailroom: "Tell me whenever a red letter shows up or goes away." Now it taps your shoulder with exactly those changes and nothing else.

sections.title: Windows with PARTIAL
sections.content:
The PARTIAL return option asks for only a slice of the results, given as a range. The first result is number 1, so PARTIAL 1:500 gets the first 500 results and PARTIAL 501:1000 the next 500. A command MUST NOT contain more than one PARTIAL or ALL option.

If the range runs past the end, the server returns what exists. A range wholly beyond the end gets NIL. Clients may ask for windows in any order. Because mailboxes change, clients often combine PARTIAL with UPDATE when walking a large result set, but the two do not interact, so the client may be told about changes to messages outside its window.

Servers MAY cache results to make later searches cheaper, but they MUST behave the same whether or not a cache is used, so a cache has to be kept current as the mailbox changes.
sections.eli5: Instead of dumping a huge pile on your desk, the clerk hands you 500 letters at a time, and you can ask for any batch you like.

sections.title: Recipes from the Cookbook
sections.content:
The appendix shows how to combine the options.

  • Virtual mailbox: select the real mailbox, then switch to a filtered view with RETURN (COUNT UPDATE CONTEXT) and fetch windows with PARTIAL as the user scrolls.
  • Trash view: a search for DELETED gives a trash-like view, and UNDELETED gives its opposite.
  • Immediate expunge notice: SEARCH RETURN (UPDATE) ALL reports expunged messages at once without changing sequence numbers until the normal EXPUNGE.
  • Monitoring counts: SEARCH RETURN (UPDATE COUNT) FLAGGED UNANSWERED lets a client track a count without holding any results.
  • Resynchronizing: the simplest way is to recreate the context, which can be done in one round-trip.
sections.eli5: These are ready-made recipes, like a folder for trash or a counter that tells you how many unanswered flagged letters you have.

sections.title: Security and Server Costs
sections.content:
The RFC says it adds capabilities and so does not change the underlying IMAP security considerations, and the authors and reviewers believe no new security issues are introduced. It does warn that creating a large number of contexts may offer authorized users a way to mount a denial-of-service attack.

Implementors can limit how many contexts may be created using the refusal mechanism, reduce their cost with the implementation strategies in Appendix B, and log context creation and use so administrators can respond. Appendix B notes that a server can handle updates by testing new messages and flag changes against each stored search, and that updating contexts for SORT will almost certainly need a results cache.
sections.eli5: If someone asks the mailroom to watch thousands of lists at once, it gets overworked, so the mailroom is allowed to say no.

data.title: Search with live updates
data.code:
C: B01 UID SEARCH RETURN (UPDATE COUNT) DELETED
   KEYWORD $Junk
S: * ESEARCH (TAG "B01") COUNT 74
S: B01 OK Search completed, will notify.
[...]
S: * ESEARCH (TAG "B01") UID ADDTO (0 32768:32769)
[...]
S: * ESEARCH (TAG "B01") UID REMOVEFROM (0 32768)
